docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A block diagram defines the system architecture of a circuit by mapping signal and power pathways across the design. The diagram identifies the system power source and distributed power levels, maps the signal integration of all sensors and actuators, and highlights key team connections for the addition of other subsystems.

docs.title: 1. 5V Voltage Regulator Module
docs.text:
1. L7805ABV-DG (STMicroelectronics 5V 1.5A Linear Regulator)

    • $0.88 / each
    • STMicroelectronics L7805ABV-DG Datasheet
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Already available on hand (zero additional cost) Requires thermal consideration under high current draw TO-220 package allows easy breadboard and through-hole PCB assembly Linear topology dissipates excess voltage (\(9\text{V} \rightarrow 5\text{V}\)) as heat Provides stable \(5\text{V DC}\) output up to \(1.5\text{A}\), fully powering the PIC18, LM324, and speaker driver

  2. LM2596S-5.0 (Texas Instruments Buck Switching Regulator)

    • $2.50 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Highly efficient (\(>80\%\)) switching conversion Requires external power inductor, catch diode, and filter capacitors Low heat generation under heavy load Higher component count and complex PCB layout footprint

  3. UA78M05CKCS (Texas Instruments 5V 500mA Linear Regulator)

    • $0.72 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Standard TO-220 through-hole footprint Lower current capacity (\(500\text{mA}\)) compared to L7805 Inexpensive and reliable Marginally lower thermal overhead

Choice: Option 1: STMicroelectronics L7805ABV-DG

Rationale: The L7805ABV-DG is already on hand. Because the subsystem consumes under \(300\text{mA}\) total continuous current, power dissipation across the regulator is well within safe operating parameters for the TO-220 through-hole package without needing an extra heatsink.

docs.title: 2. Microcontroller Platform
docs.text:
1. PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Board

    • Pre-selected Course Requirement
    • PIC18F57Q43 Hardware User Guide
    Pros Cons Required development platform for EGR304 DIP/through-hole header style occupies larger PCB footprint On-board PKOB4 programmer/debugger over USB Integrated \(12\text{-bit}\) ADC (ADC1), \(8\text{-bit}\) DAC, Configurable Logic Cells (CLC), and PWM peripherals

Choice: Option 1: Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Board

Rationale: Core processing board for all team subsystems.

docs.title: 3. Motion / Pet Detection Sensor
docs.text:
1. OPB732 Reflective Optical Sensor

    • $4.61 / each
    • Datasheet
    • DigiKey Product Page
Pros Cons Integrated IR LED and phototransistor in a single enclosed housing prevent ambient light false triggers Higher per-unit cost than bare IR emitters/receivers Direct \(5\text{V}\) rail compatibility allows simple \(17.3\text{mA}\) drive via a standard \(220\Omega\) resistor (\(R2\)) Requires discrete external load/pull-down resistors for signal conditioning Wide output voltage swing (\(0\text{V}\rightarrow 5\text{V}\)) provides excellent noise immunity for op-amp filtering Fixed optimum sensing range (\(0.10^{\prime\prime}\text{--}0.50^{\prime\prime}\)) requires precise physical mounting 24-inch 26 AWG wire leads and snap-in panel housing simplify chassis mounting

  1. Photoresistor / Light Dependent Resistor (LDR)

    • $0.00 (Included in provided electronics kit, Item 18)
    • Generic CdS Photoresistor
    Pros Cons On hand; simple voltage divider interface with a \(10\text{k}\Omega\) resistor Sensitive to ambient room lighting variations; requires calibration Detects light blockage when a pet approaches the feeding dish Slower optical response time (\(20\text{--}30\text{ms}\))

  2. Adafruit 4666 Mini Basic PIR Sensor (BS412 Element)

    • $1.95 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Inexpensive miniature PIR element Requires external bias resistors and driver circuitry Ultra-compact metal CAN TO-5 package footprint Shorter detection range (\(3\text{m}\)) compared to full modules

Choice: OPB732 Reflective Optical Sensor

Rationale: The TT Electronics OPB732 reflective optical switch was selected for subsystem to provide reliable, non-contact motion and position sensing while maintaining clean integration with the central microcontroller architecture, while also having a proof on concept of function as it was used in a previous lab.

docs.title: 4. Signal Conditioning (Op-Amp)
docs.text:
1. LM324N Quad General Purpose Operational Amplifier

    • $0.82 / each
    • TI LM324N Datasheet
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons On hand; 14-pin DIP through-hole package Not a true rail-to-rail output swing (max output \(\approx V_{CC} - 1.5\text{V}\)) Four independent channels allow scaling multiple sensor inputs Higher offset voltage compared to modern precision op-amps Operates directly from a single \(+5\text{V}\) supply rail

  2. LMC6484IN/NOPB (Texas Instruments CMOS Quad Rail-to-Rail Op-Amp)

    • $2.35 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons True rail-to-rail input and rail-to-rail output (RRIO) capability Higher unit price than basic general-purpose op-amps Low input bias current (\(20\text{fA}\)) and single \(+5\text{V}\) supply operation Requires separate purchase and shipping 14-pin DIP through-hole package compatible with breadboard testing

  3. MCP6004-E/P (Microchip Low-Power Quad Op-Amp)

    • $0.98 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Rail-to-rail I/O optimized for \(1.8\text{V}\text{--}5.5\text{V}\) single-supply circuits Lower gain-bandwidth product (\(1\text{MHz}\)) Standard 14-pin DIP through-hole package Requires additional order

Choice: Option 1: Texas Instruments LM324N

Rationale: The LM324N is currently on hand in a DIP-14 package. Configured as a non-inverting buffer/comparator, it conditions auxiliary analog sensor signals into the PIC18F57Q43 RA0 (ADC1) input within the \(0\text{--}3.5\text{V}\) dynamic range without requiring external purchases.

docs.title: 5. Audio Alert Output
docs.text:
1. Soberton Inc. PT-1407 Piezoelectric Transducer

    • $1.18 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Standard \(5\text{V}\) operating rating with minimal power consumption (\(1\text{mA}\)) Plays narrower acoustic frequency bands compared to dynamic speakers High acoustic intensity output (\(80\text{dB}\) at \(10\text{cm}\)) Requires PWM square wave driving signal from MCU Compact 13.8mm through-hole PC pin footprint

  2. 8-Ohm Dynamic Speaker + PN2222A NPN Driver Stage

    • $0.00 (On hand component & Kit NPN Transistor, Item 10)
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons On hand; capable of playing complex multi-tone audio meal chimes via PWM Requires transistor driver stage (PN2222A) due to low coil impedance (\(8\Omega\)) Richer tone and higher acoustic output than a piezo buzzer Draws higher peak current (\(\approx 100\text{mA}\)) during tone generation

  3. TDK PS1240P02BT (Piezoelectric Audio Indicator)

    • $0.73 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Compact 12.2mm through-hole footprint Plays single-frequency high-pitched tones only Low operating current draw (\(<5\text{mA}\)) Requires separate order and shipping time

Choice: Option 1: Soberton Inc. PT-1407 Piezoelectric Transducer

Rationale: The Soberton Inc. PT-1407 is selected for its compact 13.8mm through-hole footprint, low \(1\text{mA}\) operating current draw at \(5\text{V}\), and \(80\text{dB}\) sound output. Driven directly by the PIC18 microcontroller PWM pin (RA1), it eliminates the need for a transistor driver stage while providing an audible alert chime when feeding routines are triggered.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is designed to support a non-contact optical sensing and signal-processing subsystem powered by a regulated 9V DC supply. Power enters through the J1 barrel jack—protected at the input entry point by a 0.5A inline fuse (F1) and decoupled via C1 (0.33uF)—before being stepped down to a stable +5V rail using an L7805 linear voltage regulator with output filtering (C2, 0.1uF). The system is controlled by a high-performance PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller, which interacts with an onboard debug interface consisting of a pushbutton switch on RD1 and a current-limited status LED on RD0. Functionally, the system continuously monitors target proximity using an OPB732 reflective optical switch driven at approx. 17.3mA via R2 (220 ohm). The sensor's phototransistor output is conditioned through an LM324N operational amplifier buffer to provide a clean analog voltage swing into the PIC's RA0 ADC input pin (Pin 43) for software decoding and real-time serial debug logging to PuTTY via CDC_TX/CDC_RX. Upon detecting an active event, the microcontroller triggers local audible feedback via a PT-1407 piezo buzzer on PWM pin RA1 while simultaneously asserting digital pin RD2 (Pin 22) to send a high-level trigger pulse out through inter-board header J3 (Pin 1) to drive the downstream motor subsystem.
